notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, the largest (agree 0.84): for template and principle statements one coder used course-start/general where the other used during-work; resolved by whether the sentence governs doing the work (during-work), states a standing principle or fact (general), or communicates expectations (course-start). (2) unit_stance on disclosure, citation and verification duties (A permit/neutral, B require/neutral): resolved to permit for disclosure and citation, which attach a condition to allowed AI use, and neutral for verification duties, since none of these requires using AI. (3) actor and modality on single sentences (researchers, admin vs all, informs vs should for 'encourages', must-not vs should-not for advice on personal data), resolved from the sentence's wording. (4) Type: discrimination ban (P77 with fit_note), concern path for people affected by AI-supported decisions and 'never a substitute for peer-reviewed research' (both UNCOVERED, merged notes), template-2 per-assignment permission (P04 over P107), assignment-description expectations (P09 over P04). (5) Unit boundaries: several anchors landed on different parts of the same passage and were matched by passage (e.g. A0/B2, A8/B12, A15/B19, A16/B13, A18/B22, A24/B21); coder B split the 12 listed purposes in template 3 and several extra sentences, all kept (22 B-only kept); 5 A-only kept; 2 A-only dropped (assignment-description list item already inside the P09 unit's policy; infosec 'following general categories' lead-in with no categories in the saved text). Stance agreed in all 3 documents (permit, delegates, permit). new_types empty on both sides. unit_stance agreement is not reported in the schema; it was the most frequent field disagreement after phase.
